leading_candidate_selected: M5_REFINED — Patient-specific sleep-state venous-pressure-aware adaptive drainage

why_M5_REFINED_leading: PASSES physics pre-check (sleep-state ICP variation + venous congestion well-documented, magnitude 5-15 mmHg clinically consequential)
PASSES physiology pre-check (sleep apnea → venous congestion → reduced CSF-venous pressure differential → inadequate drainage during sleep is eShunt-specific physiology)
Has eShunt-specific novel angle (venous sinus pressure varies during sleep apnea — NOT present in VP shunts which drain to peritoneum where sleep-state venous pressure is irrelevant)
Lower prior-art saturation than M8 (M8 has 5+ direct hits on non-invasive ICP monitoring)
Lower novelty concern than M4 (M4 has near-direct hits on CSF production-rate measurement/regulation: US8109899B2 Likvor, US11173289B2 CSF Refresh)
Patient-specific calibration element (individual sleep-state venous pressure profile)
Clear clinical problem (nocturnal over-drainage is documented VP shunt complication)
leading_candidate_rationale.leading_candidate_definition: An eShunt with integrated (a) posture/activity sensor (accelerometer/IMU), (b) circadian clock, (c) optional sleep apnea detector (SpO2 or nasal pressure), (d) adaptive drainage controller that modulates drainage resistance based on patient-specific sleep-state venous pressure profile. The patient-specific calibration is established during a 1-7 day monitoring period post-implantation, then the controller operates autonomously. KEY DISTINCTION FROM VIEshunt: eShunt-specific venous pressure compensation (VP shunts do not have a venous pressure component because they drain to peritoneum).
